classification.difficultyReason: Find an intermediate squared length, use the equal-side marks, then apply Pythagoras again.

content.prompt: Find the length of $AD$ in the diagram below.

spec.description: Joined right triangles BCD and ABD. BC and AD are vertical; CD is horizontal. Double ticks identify AB = BD. Ordinary source blue edges are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: BC = CD = 2 m; angle BCD = angle ABD = 90 degrees; AB = BD. Required length AD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths, vertex labels, equality ticks and right-angle markers are visible.

answer.short:
$4\text{ m}$.

Apply Pythagoras in $BCD$, then use $AB=BD$ in $ABD$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $BCD$:
$$\begin{align*}BD^2&=2^2+2^2\\BD^2&=8.\end{align*}$$
The matching ticks show that $AB=BD$, so $AB^2=8$. In right-angled triangle $ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}AD^2&=AB^2+BD^2\\AD^2&=8+8\\AD^2&=16\\AD&=4\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
